question.leadin: This dynasty converted the Schonbrunn (shurn-brun) Palace from a hunting lodge to the permanent imperial summer residence where Franz Joseph died.
question.text: Name this dynasty that inbred so much they developed a namesake chin. Under this dynasty's Charles V, their empire stretched from Spain to Hungary.
question.clue: The founder of this house gained significant parcels of land after his victory at the Battle of Marchfeld, and the death of a later member of this house served as the extinction of its non-Styrian branch.

swap.text: A famous part of the army of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth were the Winged Hussars, an elite cavalry unit that lifted the Ottoman siege of this present-day European country's capital city of Vienna.
swap.clue: A United Nations Secretary General from this country received a telegram from Idi Amin that praised the Munich Massacre during his service from 1972 to 1981.

question.leadin: His death and that of his wife Sophie prompted the July Crisis.
question.text: Name this heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne whose assassination in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip helped lead to the outbreak of World War I.
question.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

swap.leadin: The fates of the remnants of both the Holy Roman Empire and post-Napoleonic France were debated in this city.
swap.text: Name this Austrian city, site of an 1814-1815 Congress.
swap.clue: This event saw Krakow become a free city, and the Earl of Clancarty replaced Castlereagh as England's representative to this event.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some of the Revolutions of 1848.
question.text: The Revolutions of 1848 shattered the delicate Concert of Europe established by this Austrian statesman to restore the European balance of power at the Congress of Vienna, which this leader hosted.
question.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Zionist Movement.
swap.text: This man declared that the Dreyfus Affair inspired him to establish the World Zionist Organization that encourages Jewish immigration to Palestine.
swap.clue: With Max Norday, this man established the Basel Program, through which the Russian faction shot down the Uganda Plan put forward by this man.

question.leadin: This empire was founded in the 1867 Ausgleich ("OWSS-glykh") and was dissolved in the Treaties of Saint Germain and Trianon ("TREE-uh-non").
question.text: Name this empire that was first ruled by Franz Josef I.
question.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary [or Austro-Hungarian Empire or Österreichisch-Ungarische Monarchie or Osztrák-Magyar Monarchia; prompt on dual monarchy; do not accept “Austria” or “Hungary” alone]
question.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

swap.leadin: This empire used "K.U.K." as its official abbreviation on ships and various articles of state in order to reflect political realities of split power.
swap.text: Name this European empire that was formed by a namesake 1867 compromise. It was one of the members of the pre-World War I Triple Alliance along with Italy and the German Empire.
swap.clue: The phrase "k.u.k" was used as a term for this country's system of government after the Ausgleich.

question.text: This author of Der Judenstaat opposed the Uganda Project and established the First Zionist Congress.
question.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

swap.leadin: This city's fin-de-siecle(fan duh SYECK-luh) culture involved many discussions in coffeehouses, and is the subject of a book by Karl Schorske.
swap.text: Name this city once governed by Karl Lueger, who declared "it is up to me to decide who is a Jew."
swap.clue: One event in this city was interrupted by the Hundred Days.

question.leadin: A rigged referendum used to bring about this event featured a ballot with a large, centered "yes" circle and a smaller "no" circle to the right.
question.text: Name this 1938 event in which Nazi Germany annexed its southern neighbor. Kurt Schuschnigg ("SHOOSH-nig") was forced to resign for opposing this event.
question.answerHtml: Anschluss (“ON-sh’loose”) [prompt on, but DO NOT REVEAL, descriptions like German annexation of Austria]
question.clue: Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about lesser-known "Wars of Succession" from European history.
swap.text: The War of Bavarian Succession saw this Habsburg co-regent of his mother, Maria Theresa, lead his men in the field in Bavaria against Frederick the Great's men, with the Peace of Teschen seeing a small territorial gain for Austria.
swap.clue: The army of this king supposedly attacked itself instead of the Turkish army during the Battle of Karansebes.

question.text: The Manila galleon trade was established under the rule of this dynasty, whose first Spanish King was Charles I. This longtime ruling house of Austria was replaced in Spain by the Bourbon Dynasty.
question.clue: In the 19th century, this family took the title "King of Lombardy-Venetia".

swap.text: To help reconstruct Portugal's social structure after the earthquake, a queen regent with this name founded the Casa Pia children's educational institution. A later Braganza queen of this name was similarly known as "The Educator."
swap.answerHtml: Maria [or Maria the Pious; or Maria the Mad; or Dona Maria I; or Maria the Good Mother; or Dona Maria II]

question.text: The Nazi-Austria fun house continued with the affair named for this politician, who served as UN Secretary General from 1972 to 1981. He was discovered to have lied about his Nazi past during his 1986 election campaign.
question.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

swap.text: Problems in the Balkans eventually led to the assassination of this heir to the Hapsburg throne in Sarajevo in 1914.
swap.clue: It's 1914. You are a Bosnian Serb and member of the Black Hand Gavrilo Princip, who will assassinate this Archduke and his wife Sophie, setting off a chain of events that will begin World War I.

question.leadin: After the Irish-born officer Maximilian Karl Lamoral O'Donnell thwarted an assassination attempt against this emperor, his brother raised funds to build the Votive Church to thank God for saving his life.
question.text: Name this emperor whose foreign minister Count Leopold Berchtold issued an ultimatum to Serbia on the eve of World War 1. He was part of the Three Emperors' League with Kaiser Wilhelm I and Tsar Alexander II.
question.answerHtml: Franz Joseph I [or Francis Joseph I; prompt on Franz Joseph; prompt on Francis Joseph]
question.clue: The Fundamental Articles of his minister of commerce and agriculture Albert Schaffle was denounced by German nationalists, and he appeared beside Alexander II in Berlin in 1873 in support of the Dreikaiserbund.

swap.leadin: This son of Leopold II was named commander-in-chief of the Austrian army in 1806.
swap.text: Name this winner over Andre Massena at First Zurich. More famously, he became the first person to beat Napoleon in over a decade when he beat Napoleon at Aspern-Essling.

question.leadin: After this event, Count Eduard Taaffe claimed that a man died "due to a rupture of an aneurism of the heart."
question.text: What event was a murder-suicide in which a man shot his lover, Mary Vetsera, and then killed himself while staying at a hunting lodge in the village that lends its name to this event?
question.clue: Ida von Ferenczy was drafted to break the news of this event to Empress Elizabeth.

swap.text: In the years leading up to World War I, the Austro-Hungarian military Chief of Staff was this bonehead, who got Austria to declare war on Serbia and then screwed up basically everything in the first half of the war.
swap.answerHtml: Franz Conrad von Hoetzendorf [or Franz Xaver Josef Conrad von Hoetzendorf; accept von Hoetzendorf]
